title: What If Your Mail Came by Cruise Missile? In 1959 It Did

scenes.text: What if your mail arrived by cruise missile? In 1959, three thousand letters did.
On June eighth, the submarine USS Barbero carried a Regulus missile about a hundred miles out to sea.
The space built for a nuclear warhead held two red and blue boxes, stamped US Mail.
Just before noon it fired. Twenty-two minutes later the missile landed at a naval air station in Florida.
The Postmaster General promised missile mail from New York to California within hours, before anyone reached the Moon.
It never flew again. Men walked on the Moon ten years later. Your letter still takes days.

description:
What if your mail arrived by cruise missile? On 8 June 1959 the US Post Office and the Navy tried it: the submarine USS Barbero fired a Regulus I missile whose warhead space held two containers with 3,000 letters, and 22 minutes later it landed at the naval air station at Mayport, Florida.
Postmaster General Arthur Summerfield predicted that before man reached the Moon, mail would cross the country and the oceans within hours by guided missile. It was the only missile mail flight the United States ever made; the Smithsonian's postal museum reads it as a Cold War signal of how accurately a missile could be aimed.
